newsitem.title: TURKEY: Mayor's brother abducted in southeast Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Mayor's brother abducted in southeast Turkey.

text.p: The mayor of a town in Turkey's troubled southeast said on Thursday that his younger brother had been abducted at the beginning of the week.
"We do not know yet who kidnapped my brother and why. I have not heard anything from him since then," Behcet Bekdas, mayor of the Lice, 80 km (50 miles) north of Diyarbakir, told Reuters
The mayor said his brother, Abdulselam Bektas, was taken away from home by five armed men in military uniform on Monday. "They told his family they will free him after fifteen minutes," he said.
An investigation has been continuing about the kidnap, an official of the emergency rule governer's office, based in Diyarbakir, said.
A Turkish human rights group said last week that security forces had threatened to raze the town of Lice and kill its inhabitants if they did not join an anti-rebel "village guard" militia.

Police in Lice kicked and punched some members of a rights group who went to the town on Monday to investigate the charges, witnesses said. Police also accused members of the group of supporting the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), the witnesses said.
More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old conflict between the security forces and the PKK rebels, fighting for autonomy or independence in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
More than 70,000 mainly Kurdish village guards are enrolled to help the government in the fight against the guerrillas.
